newsitem.title: ITALY: ENI,Enel seen in electricity deal.
newsitem.headline: ENI,Enel seen in electricity deal.

text.p: Italy's state-controlled energy giant ENI and electricity utility Enel are due to form a joint venture to produce electricity, Italian press said on Sunday.

Milan daily Corriere della Sera said the two groups were due to sign a letter of intent on Monday to set up a 50-50 percent owned company creating Italy's second largest electricity producer after Enel.

ENI managing director Franco Bernabei was quoted as saying at the weekend that ENI's goal was not to simply to enter the electric energy business "which in Italy is a saturated market," but to be able to supply the ENI group's oil refineries and chemical plants "with energy at a highly competitive cost."

Details of the deal have not yet been revealed, but the plan, for which both ENI and Enel confirmed in March that talks were already underway, is likely to involve the combining of certain already existing power plants from both groups.

Corriere said the resulting company, likely to seek a Bourse listing and possible other private partners, should be one equipped with combined-cycle (gas and coal) power plants with installed potential of some 4,000 Megawatts.
Italy's current second biggest electricity producer, the private company Edison, part of the Montedison group, has installed power of 3,200 Megawatts.

Corriere noted that to become fully operative, the new joint venture will have to await the final outcome of government measures to liberalise and regulate Italy's electricity sector in light of Enel's planned future privatisation, as well as the implementation of European Union liberalisation directives.

Newspapers reported this weekend that the Italian Treasury, which currently holds 69 percent of ENI, has decided to place a third tranche of the energy group on the market in late June after two previous highly successful tranche sales.
